Risk title: Inaccurate AI output is acted on or sent to a customer
Risk scenario: A staff member relies on an AI summary or draft (ScribeCo, WriteCo) that misstates facts, commitments or figures, and it is sent to a customer or used in a decision, leading to a dispute, a contractual misstatement or a wrong action.
Controls credited (and why): CGI-POL-001 s4.5.3 (review before sending) credited at partial strength: approved, unevidenced, likelihood 4 -> 3. Nothing reduces impact.
Treatment: TP-11: named reviewers, review log, monthly accuracy sample (AIG-09); AI-use module (AIG-08)
Drawer-2 test: NEW. VR-006's controls govern what suppliers do with Cypher's data, not whether output is right; VR-005's govern which tools arrive; an approved tool can still be wrong.

Risk title: An AI tool is used for a prohibited or high-risk purpose without classification
Risk scenario: A team uses an approved AI tool, or switches on a supplier feature, for a purpose the AI Act bans (e.g. emotion inference from staff voices) or lists as high-risk (e.g. ranking applicants), with no classification, making Cypher liable as deployer or, under Art. 25(1)(c), as provider.
Controls credited (and why): None credited: the onboarding gate (VR-005) checks new tools, not new uses of approved ones.
Treatment: TP-12: banned-use list and intended-use field per tool (AIG-07); HR sign-off; supplier feature census (AIG-04)
Drawer-2 test: NEW. VR-005's gate is inert against a new use of an approved tool, and no other risk covers regulatory classification.
